trial_name: Lu AA21004/CCT-004, vortioxetine in major depressive disorder
sponsor: Takeda Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Lundbeck Japan K.K.

primary_publication.citation: Phase 3 study of Lu AA21004 (vortioxetine) in major depressive disorder, protocol CCT-004
primary_publication.registry_documents: Protocol and statistical analysis plan at cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/16/NCT02389816/

condition: recurrent major depressive disorder, adults 20 to 75 years, MADRS total score 26 or higher at screening and baseline
intervention: vortioxetine 10 mg or 20 mg once daily, oral

full_analysis_set.note: FAS and safety analysis set coincide; safety set is all patients who took at least one dose of blinded drug. Four randomised patients had no post-baseline assessment.

inclusion: MADRS total score 26 or higher at screening and at baseline

statistical_analysis_plan.multiplicity_method: Holm step-down, two-sided, overall type I error below 5%, applied between the two doses on the primary outcome
statistical_analysis_plan.procedure: Order the two p values. Step 1: if the smaller exceeds 0.025, testing stops and both doses are non-significant. If it is at or below 0.025, reject and proceed. Step 2: test the larger against 0.05.
statistical_analysis_plan.order_is_data_dependent: The testing order is NOT fixed in advance by dose. It is determined by the observed p values: the dose with the smaller p is tested first, whichever it turns out to be. Stating that the 20 mg dose was tested first is correct only a posteriori; presenting that order as pre-specified misdescribes the method.
statistical_analysis_plan.outcome_of_procedure: Smaller p was 0.0023 (20 mg), at or below 0.025, so it was rejected and the procedure advanced. Larger p was 0.0080 (10 mg), at or below 0.05, so it was rejected too. Both doses reached significance after adjustment.
statistical_analysis_plan.blocking_described_not_exercised: Had the smaller p exceeded 0.025, both doses would have been blocked. That did not occur. This trial describes a blocking mechanism without exercising it, and is not a source of C5.
statistical_analysis_plan.secondary_outcomes: The SAP makes no adjustment for multiplicity on the secondary outcomes. Every secondary result below is nominal or exploratory, whatever its p value.

outcomes.measure: change from baseline in MADRS total score
outcomes.analysis: mixed models for repeated measures, full analysis set
outcomes.scale_note: MADRS is a 10-item clinician-rated scale, total range 0 to 60, higher scores indicating greater severity. A negative change indicates improvement.
outcomes.status: confirmatory, both doses met after Holm adjustment

outcomes.note_10mg: does not reach nominal significance at 5%; the interval crosses zero

outcomes.note: Neither dose separates from placebo. Sign convention unverified: on the DSST a higher score indicates better performance, so a negative difference read literally is worse than placebo. Recorded as reported.

outcomes.responder_definition: a reduction of 50% or more in MADRS total score from baseline
outcomes.note: per-arm proportions not extracted; only the odds ratio is in hand

adverse_events.scope_declaration: Only overall incidence and discontinuation due to a treatment-emergent adverse event are carried here. Per-term frequencies were not extracted: the source names nausea as the most common event with a dose-response relationship, and lists nasopharyngitis, headache, dizziness, somnolence and diarrhoea above 5%, without per-arm counts in hand. A summary generated from this table cannot report per-term adverse event frequencies.

denominators.note: the registry discontinuation percentages use the randomised placebo n of 164, not the FAS n of 161

events.term: discontinuation due to a treatment-emergent adverse event

events.note: low in all groups, 1.4% or less. One cerebral haemorrhage in a treatment group and one subarachnoid haemorrhage assessed as unrelated.

adverse_events.unresolved: Secondary sources report discontinuation due to adverse events as 3.3%, 4.4% and 6.4%. Those figures are not reproducible from the counts above under any denominator in this table, and the explanation offered for them (exposure-time adjustment) would yield a rate per patient-year, not a percentage. The registry counts and percentages are recorded; the divergent figures are noted and not resolved.

extraction_gaps: per-term adverse event counts by arm
per-arm proportions for MADRS response and remission
